chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn 'Uthman from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) when he was asked about a man who bought a female slave, then had intercourse with her before she completed her 'iddah (waiting period for pregnancy verification). He said: 'What a bad thing he did; he should seek Allah's forgiveness and not repeat it.'

I said: And if he sold her to another, and did not complete her 'iddah, then the second owner sold her to another man, and he had intercourse with her and did not complete her 'iddah, and her pregnancy became evident with the third owner?

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The child belongs to the one with the bed (the last owner who had intercourse), and to the adulterer is the stone (if he is free, he pays a fine; if slave, he is flogged).'

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: the child belongs to the one with the bed (last owner)
key_terms.اِسْتَبْرَاءُ الرَّحِمِ: verification of pregnancy/waiting period for slave
key_terms.لِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ: to the adulterer is the stone (fine/flogging)

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a female slave's child when she is sold multiple times and has intercourse with different owners?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-waladu lil-firash* (the child belongs to the bed) within the context of *kitabah* and slave ownership, a key area of Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the minor sin of premature intercourse before the full *istibra'* period—requiring repentance—and the definitive legal attribution of lineage to the final owner who consummates the relationship. This ruling ensures social stability by anchoring paternity to the primary male figure in the domestic sphere, even in complex chains of sale.
